t: A totalitarian dictatorship under Adolf Hitler that replaced the Weimar Republic within months of January 1933.
It rearmed, annexed Austria and the Sudetenland, and launched the Second World War by invading Poland in 1939.
It murdered some six million Jews in the Holocaust and was destroyed by total military defeat in May 1945.
dyk: Hitler never formally abolished the Weimar constitution: the Enabling Act of 1933 was renewed by the Reichstag in 1937 and 1939 and extended by decree in 1943.
ev: Hitler is appointed chancellor; the Enabling Act lets his cabinet make laws without parliament
On Hindenburg’s death Hitler merges the offices of president and chancellor as Führer
The Nuremberg Laws strip German Jews of citizenship
Germany annexes Austria and, after the Munich Agreement, the Sudetenland
Germany invades Poland on 1 September, starting the Second World War in Europe
Operation Barbarossa: Germany invades the Soviet Union
The Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad
Hitler kills himself on 30 April; Germany surrenders unconditionally on 8 May
